pickToStart: Choose a conversation on the left, or search across all of them.
recoveredPreview: Recovered preview — the file itself is not in this archive
couldNotRead: The archive could not be read.
searchUnavailable: This archive was opened without a search index, so only conversation names can be searched.
chooseHelp: Pick whichever describes what you have. Nothing is decided yet, and you can come back and change your mind.
routeBackup: My iPhone is backed up to this computer.
routeBackupHelp: Amberkeep looks at the backups Finder or iTunes has already made and takes the messages out of one. The backup itself is not changed.
routeAndroidHelp: Amberkeep shows you how to make an encrypted backup on the phone, copy it here and unlock it. Four short steps on the phone, then one here.
routeFileHelp: A decrypted msgstore.db from an Android phone, or a ChatStorage.sqlite from an iPhone backup.
workspaceExtract: The messages are copied out of the backup into this folder, as ChatStorage.sqlite, with a search index beside it. Nothing in the backup itself is changed.
workspaceDecrypt: The unlocked database is written into this folder, as msgstore.db, with a search index beside it. The file you copied off the phone is not changed.
workspaceNeeded: Say where the files should go before going on.
backupsHelp: These are the iPhone backups already on this computer. The most recent one holds the most messages.
backupsNone: No iPhone backup was found on this computer.
backupsNoneHelp: Connect the iPhone with a cable, open Finder and choose the phone in the sidebar. Choose to back up all of the data on the iPhone to this Mac, leave “Encrypt local backup” unticked, and click Back Up Now. Then come back here.
backupsNowhere: This computer cannot make or restore an iPhone backup.
backupsNowhereHelp: Apple's Finder, iTunes and Apple Devices are made for macOS and Windows only, so there is nowhere on this computer for an iPhone backup to be. You can still point Amberkeep at a backup folder copied from a Mac or a Windows PC.
backupsProblem: Amberkeep was not able to look at the backups.
backupsFullDisk: On macOS the backups sit in a folder no program may read until you allow it. Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Full Disk Access. Switch on whatever you started Amberkeep from: Terminal, or Amberkeep itself. Quit that program completely and start it again — the permission only takes effect on a fresh start.
backupEncrypted: Encrypted, so it cannot be opened
backupEncryptedWhy: This backup is locked with a password. Amberkeep does not have it, cannot work it out, and will not ask you for it.
backupEncryptedFix: In Finder, choose the phone in the sidebar and untick “Encrypt local backup”. Finder asks for the old password before it will let you. Your chats are not affected by this: it changes how the backup is stored, not what is in it.
backupEncryptedWarn: Copy the backup you already have somewhere safe first. Finder keeps one backup per phone, and the next one replaces it.
androidStep1a: On the phone, open WhatsApp. Go to Settings, then Chats, then Chat backup, then End-to-end encrypted backup.
androidStep1b: Turn it on. WhatsApp offers you a password or a 64-digit key: choose the 64-digit key.
androidStep1c: A password cannot be used here. WhatsApp checks the password on the phone and only then hands the key to the app, so the key never leaves the phone and nothing on this computer can work it out from the password.
androidNext1: What you will see next: WhatsApp shows you a key of 64 characters and asks you to save it.
androidStep2a: Write the key down, or copy it somewhere you can reach from this computer. It is 64 characters, shown in eight groups of eight.
androidStep2b: Spaces and line breaks between the groups do not matter. Amberkeep ignores them.
androidNext2: What you will see next: WhatsApp asks you to confirm that you have saved the key, and then goes back to the backup screen.
androidStep3a: On the Chat backup screen, tap Back Up, and wait until it says it has finished. A long history takes a while, and stopping half way leaves nothing usable.
androidNext3: What you will see next: the screen says when the last backup finished and how big it was.
androidStep4Title: Copy the file to this computer
androidStep4a: Connect the phone and open Android/media/com.whatsapp/WhatsApp/Databases on the phone's own storage. Copy msgstore.db.crypt15 to this computer.
androidStep4b: The files whose names begin msgstore-increment are pieces of a later backup and are no use on their own. You only need msgstore.db.crypt15.
androidNext4: What you will see next: one file, usually a few hundred megabytes, depending on how much the phone has kept.
androidFileLabel: Where msgstore.db.crypt15 is on this computer
androidKeyStays: The key stays on this computer. It goes to the Amberkeep program running on this machine and nowhere else, it is never written to a file, and it never appears in a log.
keyNeeded: Type the key before going on.
keyNotAKey: That is not a 64-digit key. A key is 64 characters made only of the numbers 0 to 9 and the letters a to f, usually shown in eight groups of eight.
fileNeeded: Say where the file is before going on.
chooseInto: where to put the changed backup
fileTitle: Open a file you already have
fileHelp: A decrypted msgstore.db from an Android phone, or a ChatStorage.sqlite from an iPhone backup. Amberkeep works out which it is; the name does not have to be right.
fileLabel: The full path to the file
workingExtracting: Taking the messages out of the backup.
workingPreparing: Building the indexes that make it quick to read.
workingLocal: All of this is happening on this computer. Nothing is being uploaded and nothing is being sent anywhere.
couldNotAsk: Amberkeep could not be reached. It may have been closed.
contactsLabel: An address book, if you have one (optional)
contactsHint: A .vcf file exported from your contacts, or WhatsApp's own wa.db from the same phone. Without one, conversations are named by phone number. Amberkeep works out which kind of file it is.
noImporter: This build of Amberkeep can only open a file you already have.
noImporterHelp: It was built without the part that reads phone backups, so there is nothing here to look through. If you have a decrypted msgstore.db or a ChatStorage.sqlite already, it can open that.
openAFileInstead: Open a file I already have
androidKeyOrFile: If you saved the key into a file, the path to that file works here too.
correctAndTryAgain: Correct whatever was wrong below and try again.
fileWrites: The file itself is never changed. A search index is written beside it, in the same folder, so that searching is quick; if that folder cannot be written to, the archive still opens and searching is simply turned off.
notAffiliated: Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to WhatsApp LLC or Meta Platforms, Inc.
freeSoftware: Amberkeep's engine is free software under the AGPL-3.0. The source is at github.com/jferrl/amberkeep.
routeMigrate: I want to move an Android history onto my iPhone.
routeMigrateHelp: Amberkeep adds the Android messages to a copy of an iPhone backup, checks every one of them, and tells you how to restore it. It never touches the phone.
migrateUnproven: No backup Amberkeep has produced has yet been restored to a phone.
migrateUnprovenHelp: Everything it writes is checked, and the checks pass, but that is not the same thing. Read each step, and keep the safety backup it asks you to make.
migratePathsTitle: What to move, and where to
migratePathsHelp: Both of these are already on this computer. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is sent anywhere.
migrateBackupFound: Backups this computer has already made
migrateBackupHint: Pick one above. If the backup is somewhere else — an external disk, or a copy you made — type where it is.
migrateBackupHintAlone: Where Finder keeps the backup, or wherever you copied it to.
migrateRestoreElsewhere: Amberkeep can still make the changed backup here. Putting it onto the iPhone has to be done from a Mac or a Windows PC, with the backup folder copied across.
migrateAndroidHint: Usually msgstore.db. If you only have msgstore.db.crypt15, unlock it first from the first screen.
migratePairingLabel: WhatsApp's LID.sqlite from the same backup (optional)
migratePairingHint: Without it, somebody your iPhone knows by a hidden identity and your Android knows by number arrives as two conversations rather than one.
migrateGroupsHint: A group arrives without its members' own history, which is the part most likely to look wrong afterwards.
migrateHidden: Include conversations with no phone number
migrateHiddenHint: These cannot be matched to anyone already on the iPhone, so each arrives as somebody new.
migrateChecksHelp: Only some of this can be checked from here. The rest is on the next screens, and has to be done by you.
migrateChecksBlocked: This has to be put right first
migratePlanHelp: Nothing has been written. Read this, and nothing happens until you type the word below.
migrateAlready: already on the iPhone, left untouched
migrateAsText: would arrive as a line of text, not the picture itself
migrateNothingToMove: There is nothing to move: every message is already on the iPhone.
migrateAgreeHelp: Type {word} to go on. A button is a button you clicked; a word is a word you wrote, and this is the step that ends with your phone being written to.
migrateAgreeWrong: That is not the word. Type {word} exactly, in lower case.
migrateAgreeChosen: This will read {backup} and write a changed copy of it. Your iPhone is not touched.
migrateIntoLabel: Where to put the changed backup (optional)
migrateIntoHint: It has to be on the same disk as the original, so that it appears only once it is complete. Left empty, it goes beside the original.
migrateWorkingLocal: All of this is happening on this computer. Nothing is being uploaded, and the phone has not been touched.
migrateDoneTitle: There is a backup to restore
migrateDoneHelp: Your phone has not been touched. What follows is how to put this onto it, and what you will see while it happens.
guideEnglishOnly: These instructions are in English for now.
exportTitle: Keep a copy of your history
exportHelp: This writes your conversations into a folder on this computer. The archive is not changed and nothing is uploaded.
exportHTMLHelp: Opens in any browser, on any computer, with no internet and nothing to install. Pictures are inside the pages themselves. This is the one to keep.
exportTextHelp: The format WhatsApp's own “export chat” produces, so anything that reads those will read these.
exportJSONHelp: Every field recovered, for a program rather than a person. Useful to a solicitor’s software or your own scripts.
exportNoFormat: Choose at least one thing to write.
exportIntoHint: Left empty, it goes in the workspace folder Amberkeep already uses.
exportNoticesHelp: Messages about people joining, leaving, and security codes changing. Off by default: they are numerous and they are not things anybody said.
exportDoneTitle: Your history is on this computer
exportDoneHelp: It is yours now, in a form that does not need this program or any other.
exportDoneKeep: Copy that folder somewhere safe. A backup on the same computer is not a backup.
androidFileHint: The file you copied off the phone. It ends in .crypt15 and is usually a few hundred megabytes.
